title: Loneliness
definition: Loneliness is the painful experience of isolation or disconnection that God meets with His presence, His people, and the hope of belonging in Christ.
summary: God sees the lonely and brings them into His care and family.
christFocus: Jesus knew rejection and draws near to the lonely, bringing them into fellowship with God and His people.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Loneliness can happen even when people are surrounded by others. It may come through rejection, grief, disability, betrayal, singleness, relocation, family pain, or hidden suffering.

Scripture reveals that God sees the lonely. He promises His presence and places believers into a spiritual family. The Church is called to notice, welcome, and care for those who feel unseen.

Christ experienced rejection and abandonment, yet He brings His people near to God. In Him, loneliness is met with presence, belonging, and hope.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Lonely people often believe they are forgotten or unwanted. Loneliness matters because the Gospel speaks directly to the need for presence, belonging, and faithful love.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring loneliness honestly to God and resist the pull to disappear. Seek healthy fellowship, reach out to one person, and look for someone else who may need the welcome of Christ through you.
